name: Lunch Money
tagline: Import transactions and maintain a transparent personal ledger with rules and reports

tiers.name: Monthly Subscription
tiers.limits: All product features; 30-day trial; price locked for life

tiers.name: Annual Subscription
tiers.limits: All product features; user can set annual price, displayed default $100/year; 30-day trial
tiers.notes: Annual amount is user-selectable; $100/year is the displayed default, not a hard fixed price.

pricing.freeTierCaps: no free tier; 30-day trial with no credit card
pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual (annual price is user-set; displayed default $100/year)
pricing.hiddenCosts: Annual customers can choose their own price; organization pricing is separate. Pausing converts unused time into account credit.

verdictSummary: The core loop is buildable, but a dependable replacement becomes a real weekend or multi-day project. For Lunch Money, import transactions and maintain a transparent personal ledger with rules and reports. The hard boundary is bank sync, multi-currency support, api, community, and hosted convenience, plus financial integrations, compliance, and trust.
coreLoopDIY: Import transactions, categorize them with transparent rules, reconcile balances, and maintain a personal ledger with clean exported reports without moving money.
requirements: CSV or OFX exports from financial institutions
whatYouLose: bank sync, multi-currency support, API, community, and hosted convenience
replacementScope: personal ledger or simple invoicing tool
ongoingBurden: import normalization, reconciliation, rule drift, exchange rates, backups, audit trails, tax changes, bank APIs, and support
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Lunch Money because people pay because accurate money records and dependable institution connections are worth more than the visible charts. The recurring cost buys import normalization, reconciliation, rule drift, exchange rates, backups, audit trails, tax changes, bank APIs, and support, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Actual Budget
priorArt.desc: Active local-first open-source personal finance application.

alternatives.name: FreeBudget
alternatives.desc: Budgets, rules, CSV imports and net worth for free; live bank links are the one thing that sends a small bill.

facts.install: Hosted signup in a browser or installation of its progressive web app
facts.dataFormat: Transactions, budgets, rules, reports, and net-worth records live in FreeBudget's cloud; manual and CSV import/export are available, while linked-account data passes through Plaid when the paid sync option is enabled.
facts.gapVsPaid: FreeBudget's free tier omits live bank links and has a narrower API, multi-currency, rules, and transaction-management experience than Lunch Money.

alternatives.name: Actual Budget
alternatives.desc: A transparent ledger with imports, rules and reports on your own disk; automatic bank sync is optional.

facts.install: Native desktop app for local-only use, or the official Docker/Node server for browser access and device sync
facts.dataFormat: Each client works from a local SQLite budget; the server keeps account metadata plus budget blobs under its data directory, and optional end-to-end encryption covers budget contents but not bank-sync tokens.
facts.gapVsPaid: Actual provides a transparent ledger but its hosted API, multi-currency workflow, automatic aggregation, and flexible transaction-analysis experience are less turnkey than Lunch Money's.

alternatives.name: Firefly III
alternatives.desc: A meticulous imported ledger with rules and reports in Docker; powerful, private and willing to teach accounting words.

facts.install: Official Docker Compose deployment; a separate Firefly III Data Importer is normally added for bank files
facts.dataFormat: Transactions, accounts, budgets, rules, and metadata live in the configured MariaDB/MySQL or PostgreSQL database; uploads and generated files live in persistent server volumes.
facts.gapVsPaid: Firefly III is more operationally demanding and less approachable than Lunch Money for quick imports, flexible rules, multi-currency personal use, and API-driven automation.
facts.setupBlocker: The first obstacle is operating a real web service, Docker, a database, application secrets, TLS, mail, backups, upgrades, and usually the separate importer plus an API token.

alternatives.name: ezBookkeeping
alternatives.desc: A fast private ledger with absurdly broad import support, mapping rules and sharp reports; budgeting is deliberately not invited.

facts.install: Run the published Docker image/Compose file or a prebuilt server binary
facts.engines: Includes receipt-image recognition plus API, MCP, and agent integration; the official documentation does not identify a bundled general-purpose LLM backend.
facts.dataFormat: Ledger records live in the configured SQLite, MySQL/MariaDB, or PostgreSQL database; uploaded receipt images and other files remain on the server or configured object storage.
facts.gapVsPaid: ezBookkeeping deliberately omits budgeting, so it cannot replace Lunch Money's budget planning even though its private ledger, imports, and reports are strong.
facts.setupBlocker: A non-expert has to provide a server, database or persistent SQLite volume, an application secret, HTTPS, backups, and upgrades before the web and mobile clients are safely useful.

alternatives.name: Wealthfolio
alternatives.desc: Transactions, rules, spending reports and net worth on your device; automatic account sync is paid.

facts.install: Native desktop or iOS app, or the official Docker image/Compose deployment for web mode
facts.dataFormat: Desktop and self-hosted modes use a local SQLite database (the web server exposes a configurable app.db path); optional Wealthfolio Connect and encrypted device sync send selected holdings/account data through the vendor service.
facts.gapVsPaid: Wealthfolio is portfolio-centered and has thinner budgeting, recurring-expense, multi-currency transaction, and rule-management tools than Lunch Money.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Lunch Money plan and a personal ledger or simple invoicing tool DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a personal replacement for Lunch Money in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, SQLite, Drizzle ORM, and local-first encryption; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: import transactions, categorize them with transparent rules, reconcile balances, and maintain a personal ledger with clean exported reports without moving money.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Support CSV and OFX import with saved column mappings and duplicate detection.
Implement accounts, transactions, transfers, categories, payees, notes, and split transactions.
Add deterministic categorization rules whose matches can be inspected and undone.
Provide reconciliation, monthly budget, cash-flow, net-worth, and export views.
Keep an immutable import log and require explicit confirmation before destructive changes.
Encrypt local data, create automatic backups, and document restore on a fresh machine.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Deliberately leave out initiating payments or moving money.
Deliberately leave out tax, payroll, or accounting compliance guarantees.
Deliberately leave out screen-scraped bank access and commercial institution aggregation.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
